summary: payment-service's outbound mTLS client certificate (CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal) expired at 2026-04-02T12:15:00Z, so bank-partner-api rejected every outbound transfer handshake; this is the top-ranked hypothesis H1 at 0.82 confidence (high), clearly ahead of all rejected alternatives. The customer-visible payment failures never touch payment-service's inbound HTTP 5xx metric, which is structurally blind to outbound/asynchronous adapter failures, explaining the green error_rate dashboard. Evidence is tight and non-coincidental: cert-watcher WARN at 10:20:44Z predicting expiry in 115 minutes, first ERROR at 12:15:27Z naming our own client cert with 'tls: expired certificate (alert 45)', bank_api_error_rate jumping 0.2%->100% and payment_success_rate collapsing to ~2.5% in exactly the 12:15Z bucket, and p99 latency dropping 320ms->140ms (calls fail fast, not hang). Deploy- and config-change alternatives were tested and excluded (no payment-service deploy in 08:00-13:59Z; the only config change is a timeout raise that cannot produce alert 45 and has a 55-minute timing gap), and the partner-side outage hypothesis is contradicted by the log naming our expired credential and zero partner config changes. Remaining uncertainty is limited to the partner's server-side trust state and the renewal/recovery timeline, which were not observable.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Expired client mTLS certificate on payment-service's bank-partner-api path
ranked_hypotheses.statement: payment-service's outbound client certificate CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal expired at 2026-04-02T12:15:00Z, causing bank-partner-api to reject every mTLS handshake. All outbound transfer calls fail at the TLS layer, payments are marked PENDING_RETRY, and the customer-visible failure never touches payment-service's inbound HTTP 5xx metric, so the error_rate dashboard stays green.

causal_chain.claim: A client certificate used by payment-service for outbound mTLS to bank-partner-api had notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z and was never renewed (no renewal automation on this path).
A cert-watcher WARN at 10:20:44Z pre-announced the expiry; no remediation followed.
At 12:15Z the certificate expires; bank-partner-api begins rejecting the TLS handshake with 'remote error: tls: expired certificate (alert 45)'.
Every outbound transfer call fails fast at the handshake: bank_api_error_rate jumps 0.2%->100.0% and payment_success_rate collapses ~99.25%->~2.5% in the 12:15Z bucket, with first ERROR at 12:15:27Z.
Failures are marked PENDING_RETRY (payments 45f233b6, 7b4c31a9, 62f775af) on an async/adapter path, producing customer-visible fund-transfer failures.
Because the failure is on the outbound dependency call, not the inbound HTTP edge, the 'HTTP 5xx' error_rate panel never moves and stays ~0.2%.

assumptions: The cert expiry timestamp quoted in logs/telemetry is the actual cause and not coincidental with a partner-side policy change (bank-partner-api has no telemetry: tc-017/tc-021 could not confirm server-side trust config).
The client cert is provisioned/renewed outside the deployment and config-change systems, which is why no deploy or config change explains it (F16).
HIST-106 is treated as analogy, not evidence about the current incident.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Metric/scrape artifact: payment-service error_rate panel misleading (green because blind to the failing path)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The 'error_rate' panel is not stale or broken but structurally blind: it counts only inbound HTTP 5xx, so it cannot represent asynchronous transfer / outbound adapter failures. The green panel is an absence of relevant signal, not absence of errors, which masked a real internal fault.

causal_chain.claim: The error_rate metric is explicitly '% of requests (HTTP 5xx)' and did not move during the incident (stays ~0.2%).
The real failures occur on an outbound/async path (bank-partner-api call, PENDING_RETRY), invisible to that panel.
Therefore the green dashboard coexists with real payment failures.

assumptions: None about the origin -- this hypothesis describes the masking condition, not the fault origin.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: This is a contributing condition (monitoring blind spot), not the fault origin: it explains why the dashboard stayed green but not why payments failed. The origin evidence points to the expired client certificate (H1). Retained in notes rather than as a competing root cause.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Bank/PSP side outage or trust-policy change (reporter's suspicion)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The bank-partner-api (external vendor) degraded or changed its TLS trust policy (e.g. stricter CRL/OCSP enforcement, rotated server cert, server-side misconfiguration) around 12:15Z, rejecting payment-service handshakes. Customer-visible failures originate at the partner, and the partner has no telemetry into our stack, so payment-service's error_rate panel stays green.

causal_chain.claim: bank-partner-api is external, owner 'vendor', has_telemetry=false, so a partner-side fault would not surface on payment-service's edge metrics.
Partner-side degradation at ~12:15Z would reject outgoing mTLS calls, producing the same failure signature as observed.
payment-service marks affected payments PENDING_RETRY and customers see failed transfers while the HTTP 5xx panel is unchanged.

assumptions: That the observed TLS rejection is caused by server-side trust-config change rather than our credential's notAfter timestamp.
That the exact notAfter=12:15:00Z coincidence with onset is incidental.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: The error text explicitly names OUR client cert and the reason code 'tls: expired certificate (alert 45)' (F3/F4), and the onset matches our cert's notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z to the second (F13). 'alert 45' = certificate_expired, which is a statement about the client certificate we presented, not a 5xx from the partner. HIST-105 (partner 5xx) is a poor match (score 1) whereas HIST-106 (our cert expired) matches the mechanism (F14). No config/telemetry evidence points to a partner change.

ranked_hypotheses.title: cfg-2502: bank API timeout raised 3000->5000ms converting bank errors into silent stalls
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The config change cfg-2502 on payment-service raised bank.api.timeout_ms from 3000 to 5000 at 11:20Z, changing the behavior of the external bank call path so that failures are no longer surfaced on edge metrics and payments silently stall while customers see failures.

causal_chain.claim: cfg-2502 (bank.api.timeout_ms 3000->5000) was applied on payment-service at 11:20Z, the only config change scoped to the affected service, and was never rolled back.
Raising an outbound timeout can turn fast bank errors into long hangs/silent stalls that never raise payment-service's own error_rate.
Customers therefore observe failed/stalled transfers while the error-rate panel is green.

assumptions: That a timeout raise could produce a 100% bank_api_error_rate and a TLS-level rejection message.
That the 11:20Z change is causally linked to the 12:15Z onset despite a ~55 minute quiet gap.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Mechanism contradicts the evidence: the observed errors are TLS handshake rejections with 'expired certificate (alert 45)' (F3/F13), which a timeout change cannot produce, and a longer timeout would raise latency while p99_ms actually DROPS from ~320ms to ~140ms (F6) -- calls fail fast, not hang. Timing is also poor: a 55-minute quiet gap between 11:20Z and the 12:15Z onset, and the config touches no certificate material (F16).

ranked_hypotheses.title: dep-5510 settlement-service deploy via shared ledger-db/kafka degradation
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The settlement-service v1.9.0 deploy (dep-5510, new CSV exporter) at 10:30Z degraded a shared neighbour (ledger-db or kafka) or settlement processing, and payment-service's transfers failed as a side effect on a shared path, unseen by its edge error-rate metric.

causal_chain.claim: dep-5510 deployed settlement-service v1.9.0 at 10:30Z with a new CSV exporter.
settlement-service shares ledger-db/kafka with payment-service, so a resource/load impact there could propagate.
That shared impact causes payment transfers to fail while edge metrics stay green.

assumptions: That a CSV-export deploy could degrade ledger-db/kafka stress near 12:15Z, ~105 minutes after deploy.
That shared-neighbour impact would manifest as a TLS certificate error.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: The failure signature is a TLS handshake rejection naming our client cert (F3/F4), which shared DB/broker degradation cannot produce; the onset is ~105 minutes after the deploy with no evidence of shared-resource saturation, and shared neighbours would also visibly impact order-service/portfolio-service (F17). Settlement-service is not even an edge of payment-service.

facts.statement: The payment-service HTTP error_rate panel stayed ~0.2% (max 0.32%) across 11:45Z-13:59Z; its unit is explicitly '% of requests (HTTP 5xx)', so it counts only inbound edge 5xx and is blind to downstream/async failures.

payment-service's business-failure signal collapsed at the 12:15 bucket: bank_api_error_rate went from 0.2% to 100.0% and payment_success_rate from ~99.25% to ~2.5%, both holding at failed levels through 13:57Z; a narrow 120s-bucket query pins the transition between 12:13Z (0.21) and 12:15Z (100.0).

ERROR logs begin at 12:15:27Z ('payment 45f233b6 marked PENDING_RETRY: mTLS handshake with bank-partner-api rejected') and continue to 13:58:39Z with 311 matched lines; dominant patterns are mTLS handshake rejections (140) and 'bank-partner-api call failed: remote error: tls: expired certificate (alert 45)' (171) naming CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal.

The failure is on the outbound bank-partner-api adapter path, not inbound client HTTP: logs name 'bank-partner-api call failed' and 'mTLS handshake with bank-partner-api rejected', affected payments are marked PENDING_RETRY, and the cert notAfter timestamp 2026-04-02T12:15:00Z matches the metric onset bucket exactly.

A cert-watcher WARN at 10:20:44Z pre-signalled the expiry: 'client certificate CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal expires in 115 minutes (notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z)'; logs before 11:45Z show only 3 WARN entries and no ERRORs.

Traffic volume did not change at onset (request_rate ~100 req/s, avg 100.51), so the success collapse is not a traffic artifact; latency_p99_ms dropped from ~320ms to ~140ms at the 12:15 bucket, consistent with fast failure at the TLS handshake rather than hanging.
In 10:00Z-13:59Z the only deployment across all services was dep-5510 (settlement-service v1.9.0, 10:30Z, CSV exporter, not rolled back) - unrelated to payment-service's outbound bank path.
The only config change in the window was cfg-2502 on payment-service: bank.api.timeout_ms changed 3000->5000 at 11:20Z; it was the sole payment-service-scoped change and no rollback is recorded.
payment-service has exactly four dependency edges: ledger-db (db), bank-partner-api (external, owner 'vendor', has_telemetry false), kafka (queue-produce), and inbound from api-gateway (http).

ledger-db and kafka are shared:true multi-tenant neighbours (ledger-db used by payment-service, order-service, portfolio-service; kafka by payment-service and order-service), so degradation there would also impact other services.

Historical precedent HIST-106 (2025-06-30, match_score 5) is 'Settlement mTLS certificate expired': root cause 'Client certificate expired; no renewal automation', category credential_expiry, resolved by issuing a new cert and adding an expiry alert - the same mechanism as the current symptoms, unlike HIST-105 (match_score 1).

No deploy or config change explains the failure: ZERO deployments scoped to payment-service in 08:00Z-13:59Z, and the only payment-service config change is cfg-2502 (a timeout raise, not a cert change) - no change exists that could mint or expire a client certificate.
